## The model

The assistant is an open-weight language model with 8 billion parameters. It is stored in 4-bit precision (the term is "quantised"), which brings it down to about 5 GB of video memory. The separate model that turns documents into searchable vectors, the embedder, runs on the processor instead, so the graphics card is left free for the chat model.

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Red data.** Client contracts, personal data and financial records. It may go into Lantern only with written approval from Tomasz Lewandowski.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

**Token.** A piece of a word. Models read and write in tokens; about four characters make one token in English.

**Workspace.** A separate folder of documents and conversations for one client project. A document uploaded to one workspace cannot be seen from another.

# Lantern glossary

Short definitions of the words you will meet in the Lantern documents at Brightwater Studio.

**Amber data.** Client work in progress and internal plans. Lantern may process it. Outside AI tools may not.

**Audit log.** A record of who used Lantern, when, in which workspace and how many tokens were used. It never contains the text of a prompt or an answer. Kept for 365 days.

**Cleanup job.** The script log_cleanup.py that runs on lantern-01 every night at 02:30 and deletes chat logs and audit logs that have passed their retention period.

**Embedder.** The small model that turns a document into numbers so that Lantern can search it by meaning. It runs on the processor, not on the graphics card.

**First-token time.** How long you wait before the first word of an answer appears. The studio's target is under 3 seconds for 95 percent of requests.

**Green data.** Published or public material, such as marketing copy that is already on the website. Anyone may use it with any tool.

**Lantern.** The private AI assistant that runs on the workstation lantern-01. It is the result of Project Lantern.

**Legal hold.** An empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the cleanup job deletes nothing. Used during an incident so that evidence is kept.

**NDA.** A non-disclosure agreement. Two clients, Harbour and Pine and Corvid Foods, have NDAs that do not allow third parties to process their work.

**Pilot group.** The four people who tested Lantern from 7 April to 2 May 2025: Hannah Frost, Daniel Reyes, Samir Haddad and Leo Park.

BRIGHTWATER STUDIO
DATA HANDLING STANDARD FOR LANTERN
Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

This standard says where Lantern keeps data, how long, and how it is removed. It supports the AI use policy, which sets the rules for people. Where the two seem to differ, the policy wins and Tomasz must be told.

1. WHERE DATA LIVES

3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

    Chat logs ............................ 90 days
    Audit logs ........................... 365 days
    Uploaded documents ................... until the project is closed, plus 12 months
    Backups .............................. 30 days
    Incident records ..................... three years

3.2 A chat log is removed by the nightly retention job at 02:30, once it is more than 90 days old. Uploaded documents are not removed by the job. The operations lead, Daniel Reyes, removes them by hand when a project has been closed for 12 months, and records the date.

3.3 Because backups are kept for 30 days, a chat log that has just been deleted can still exist in a backup for up to 30 days. The longest a chat can therefore survive anywhere is 120 days.

4. LEGAL HOLD

4.1 To stop deletion during an incident, create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it is there the retention job deletes nothing.

4.2 Only Tomasz Lewandowski may order the file to be removed, after the incident review.

5. BACKUPS

5.1 A backup runs every night at 01:00 to the office NAS.

5.2 Every Sunday at 03:00 an encrypted copy goes to cloud storage in an EU region. The key stays in the office safe.

5.3 A restore is tested once a year. The first test, on 2 May 2025, restored 310 GB in 47 minutes.

6. DELETION

6.1 Deleting a file means removing it from the disk. Lantern keeps no recycle bin.

## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Red data.** Client contracts, personal data and financial records. It may go into Lantern only with written approval from Tomasz Lewandowski.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

**Token.** A piece of a word. Models read and write in tokens; about four characters make one token in English.

**Workspace.** A separate folder of documents and conversations for one client project. A document uploaded to one workspace cannot be seen from another.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

sources.text:
## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
def run(now: float | None = None) -> int:
    """Delete expired logs and return the exit code (0 normally, 3 when a legal hold is active)."""
    moment = time.time() if now is None else now
    if HOLD_FILE.exists():
        write_log("hold active, nothing deleted")
        return EXIT_HOLD
    chat = expired(CHAT_LOG_DIR, CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS, moment)
    audit = expired(AUDIT_LOG_DIR, AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS, moment)
    for path in [*chat, *audit]:
        path.unlink()
    write_log(f"deleted {len(chat)} chat logs and {len(audit)} audit logs")
    return EXIT_OK


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(run())

## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

DATA HANDLING STANDARD FOR LANTERN
Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

This standard says where Lantern keeps data, how long, and how it is removed. It supports the AI use policy, which sets the rules for people. Where the two seem to differ, the policy wins and Tomasz must be told.

1. WHERE DATA LIVES

1.1 Everything Lantern stores is on lantern-01, in the locked comms cupboard. Nothing is stored with an outside provider except the weekly encrypted backup copy (see section 5).

    - /srv/lantern/uploads holds documents that staff upload into a project workspace.
    - /srv/lantern/chat_logs holds one file per day with the conversations people had.
    - /srv/lantern/audit holds the audit log.

2.2 Every person has an individual account. Shared accounts are not allowed.

2.3 There are two administrators, Priya Nair and Tomasz Lewandowski. Both use multi-factor sign-in. Administrators can read the audit log and disable accounts. They do not read chat logs unless Tomasz opens an incident.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Red data.** Client contracts, personal data and financial records. It may go into Lantern only with written approval from Tomasz Lewandowski.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

**Token.** A piece of a word. Models read and write in tokens; about four characters make one token in English.

**Workspace.** A separate folder of documents and conversations for one client project. A document uploaded to one workspace cannot be seen from another.

sources.section: Lantern incident runbook > What to do, in order
sources.text:
## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

| When | What |

3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

    Chat logs ............................ 90 days
    Audit logs ........................... 365 days
    Uploaded documents ................... until the project is closed, plus 12 months
    Backups .............................. 30 days
    Incident records ..................... three years

3.2 A chat log is removed by the nightly retention job at 02:30, once it is more than 90 days old. Uploaded documents are not removed by the job. The operations lead, Daniel Reyes, removes them by hand when a project has been closed for 12 months, and records the date.

3.3 Because backups are kept for 30 days, a chat log that has just been deleted can still exist in a backup for up to 30 days. The longest a chat can therefore survive anywhere is 120 days.

4. LEGAL HOLD

4.1 To stop deletion during an incident, create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it is there the retention job deletes nothing.

4.2 Only Tomasz Lewandowski may order the file to be removed, after the incident review.

5. BACKUPS

5.1 A backup runs every night at 01:00 to the office NAS.

5.2 Every Sunday at 03:00 an encrypted copy goes to cloud storage in an EU region. The key stays in the office safe.

5.3 A restore is tested once a year. The first test, on 2 May 2025, restored 310 GB in 47 minutes.

6. DELETION

6.1 Deleting a file means removing it from the disk. Lantern keeps no recycle bin.

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
# Lantern glossary

Short definitions of the words you will meet in the Lantern documents at Brightwater Studio.

**Amber data.** Client work in progress and internal plans. Lantern may process it. Outside AI tools may not.

**Audit log.** A record of who used Lantern, when, in which workspace and how many tokens were used. It never contains the text of a prompt or an answer. Kept for 365 days.

**Cleanup job.** The script log_cleanup.py that runs on lantern-01 every night at 02:30 and deletes chat logs and audit logs that have passed their retention period.

**Embedder.** The small model that turns a document into numbers so that Lantern can search it by meaning. It runs on the processor, not on the graphics card.

**First-token time.** How long you wait before the first word of an answer appears. The studio's target is under 3 seconds for 95 percent of requests.

**Green data.** Published or public material, such as marketing copy that is already on the website. Anyone may use it with any tool.

**Lantern.** The private AI assistant that runs on the workstation lantern-01. It is the result of Project Lantern.

**Legal hold.** An empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the cleanup job deletes nothing. Used during an incident so that evidence is kept.

**NDA.** A non-disclosure agreement. Two clients, Harbour and Pine and Corvid Foods, have NDAs that do not allow third parties to process their work.

**Pilot group.** The four people who tested Lantern from 7 April to 2 May 2025: Hannah Frost, Daniel Reyes, Samir Haddad and Leo Park.

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

sources.title: incident-runbook.md
sources.section: Lantern incident runbook > What to do, in order
sources.text:
## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

sources.title: data-handling-standard.txt
sources.text:
3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

    Chat logs ............................ 90 days
    Audit logs ........................... 365 days
    Uploaded documents ................... until the project is closed, plus 12 months
    Backups .............................. 30 days
    Incident records ..................... three years

3.2 A chat log is removed by the nightly retention job at 02:30, once it is more than 90 days old. Uploaded documents are not removed by the job. The operations lead, Daniel Reyes, removes them by hand when a project has been closed for 12 months, and records the date.

3.3 Because backups are kept for 30 days, a chat log that has just been deleted can still exist in a backup for up to 30 days. The longest a chat can therefore survive anywhere is 120 days.

4. LEGAL HOLD

4.1 To stop deletion during an incident, create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it is there the retention job deletes nothing.

4.2 Only Tomasz Lewandowski may order the file to be removed, after the incident review.

5. BACKUPS

5.1 A backup runs every night at 01:00 to the office NAS.

5.2 Every Sunday at 03:00 an encrypted copy goes to cloud storage in an EU region. The key stays in the office safe.

5.3 A restore is tested once a year. The first test, on 2 May 2025, restored 310 GB in 47 minutes.

6. DELETION

6.1 Deleting a file means removing it from the disk. Lantern keeps no recycle bin.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

sources.text:
Memo: Which way should Brightwater 
run an AI assistant?  
To: Maya Okafor 
From: Daniel Reyes 
Date: 28 February 2025 
Decision wanted: at the kickoff meeting on 3 March 2025 
Recommendation 
I recommend Option C, a computer of our own running the assistant in the office. It is the 
most expensive of the three, but it is the only one that keeps client work inside the building, 
and two of our clients require that. 
The three options 
Option A: a cloud subscription 
Each person pays £22 per user per month. For 12 people that is £264 per month, or £3,168 
for the year. Nothing has to be bought or looked after. Our prompts and documents would 
be processed by the provider, in an EU region. 
Option B: a hosted private instance 
A provider in the UK runs an assistant for us alone at a flat £780 per month, or £9,360 for 
the year. Our data stays with that provider. Corvid Foods would have to agree to a change in 
its NDA first. 
Option C: a workstation in our own office 
A one-off cost of £2,330 (£2,150 for the workstation and £180 for a UPS battery unit) and 
£1,244 per month (a support retainer of £1,200, about £35 of electricity and £9 of cloud 
storage for backups). The first year costs £17,258. The second year would cost £14,928, 
because the one-off cost does not come back. Data never leaves the building.

Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

This standard says where Lantern keeps data, how long, and how it is removed. It supports the AI use policy, which sets the rules for people. Where the two seem to differ, the policy wins and Tomasz must be told.

1. WHERE DATA LIVES

1.1 Everything Lantern stores is on lantern-01, in the locked comms cupboard. Nothing is stored with an outside provider except the weekly encrypted backup copy (see section 5).

1.2 There are three data folders on lantern-01:
    - /srv/lantern/uploads holds documents that staff upload into a project workspace.
    - /srv/lantern/chat_logs holds one file per day with the conversations people had.
    - /srv/lantern/audit holds the audit log.

1.3 The audit log records who asked, when, in which workspace, and how many tokens the answer used. It never records the text of a prompt or of an answer.

2. ACCESS

2.1 Lantern can be reached only from the office network, subnet 192.168.10.0/24. No port is open to the internet.

2.2 Every person has an individual account. Shared accounts are not allowed.

2.3 There are two administrators, Priya Nair and Tomasz Lewandowski. Both use multi-factor sign-in. Administrators can read the audit log and disable accounts. They do not read chat logs unless Tomasz opens an incident.

3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

sources.section: Lantern incident runbook > What to do, in order
sources.text:
## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

**Token.** A piece of a word. Models read and write in tokens; about four characters make one token in English.

**Workspace.** A separate folder of documents and conversations for one client project. A document uploaded to one workspace cannot be seen from another.

## Speed

Priya measured the speed on 31 March 2025, before the pilot:

- The median time to the first word of an answer was 1.8 seconds.

sources.text:
# Lantern glossary

Short definitions of the words you will meet in the Lantern documents at Brightwater Studio.

**Amber data.** Client work in progress and internal plans. Lantern may process it. Outside AI tools may not.

**Audit log.** A record of who used Lantern, when, in which workspace and how many tokens were used. It never contains the text of a prompt or an answer. Kept for 365 days.

**Cleanup job.** The script log_cleanup.py that runs on lantern-01 every night at 02:30 and deletes chat logs and audit logs that have passed their retention period.

**Embedder.** The small model that turns a document into numbers so that Lantern can search it by meaning. It runs on the processor, not on the graphics card.

**First-token time.** How long you wait before the first word of an answer appears. The studio's target is under 3 seconds for 95 percent of requests.

**Green data.** Published or public material, such as marketing copy that is already on the website. Anyone may use it with any tool.

**Lantern.** The private AI assistant that runs on the workstation lantern-01. It is the result of Project Lantern.

**Legal hold.** An empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the cleanup job deletes nothing. Used during an incident so that evidence is kept.

**NDA.** A non-disclosure agreement. Two clients, Harbour and Pine and Corvid Foods, have NDAs that do not allow third parties to process their work.

**Pilot group.** The four people who tested Lantern from 7 April to 2 May 2025: Hannah Frost, Daniel Reyes, Samir Haddad and Leo Park.

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

DATA HANDLING STANDARD FOR LANTERN
Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.

4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

    Chat logs ............................ 90 days
    Audit logs ........................... 365 days
    Uploaded documents ................... until the project is closed, plus 12 months
    Backups .............................. 30 days
    Incident records ..................... three years

3.2 A chat log is removed by the nightly retention job at 02:30, once it is more than 90 days old. Uploaded documents are not removed by the job. The operations lead, Daniel Reyes, removes them by hand when a project has been closed for 12 months, and records the date.

3.3 Because backups are kept for 30 days, a chat log that has just been deleted can still exist in a backup for up to 30 days. The longest a chat can therefore survive anywhere is 120 days.

4. LEGAL HOLD

4.1 To stop deletion during an incident, create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it is there the retention job deletes nothing.

4.2 Only Tomasz Lewandowski may order the file to be removed, after the incident review.

5. BACKUPS

5.1 A backup runs every night at 01:00 to the office NAS.

5.2 Every Sunday at 03:00 an encrypted copy goes to cloud storage in an EU region. The key stays in the office safe.

5.3 A restore is tested once a year. The first test, on 2 May 2025, restored 310 GB in 47 minutes.

6. DELETION

6.1 Deleting a file means removing it from the disk. Lantern keeps no recycle bin.

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
# Lantern glossary

Short definitions of the words you will meet in the Lantern documents at Brightwater Studio.

**Amber data.** Client work in progress and internal plans. Lantern may process it. Outside AI tools may not.

**Audit log.** A record of who used Lantern, when, in which workspace and how many tokens were used. It never contains the text of a prompt or an answer. Kept for 365 days.

**Cleanup job.** The script log_cleanup.py that runs on lantern-01 every night at 02:30 and deletes chat logs and audit logs that have passed their retention period.

**Embedder.** The small model that turns a document into numbers so that Lantern can search it by meaning. It runs on the processor, not on the graphics card.

**First-token time.** How long you wait before the first word of an answer appears. The studio's target is under 3 seconds for 95 percent of requests.

**Green data.** Published or public material, such as marketing copy that is already on the website. Anyone may use it with any tool.

**Lantern.** The private AI assistant that runs on the workstation lantern-01. It is the result of Project Lantern.

**Legal hold.** An empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the cleanup job deletes nothing. Used during an incident so that evidence is kept.

**NDA.** A non-disclosure agreement. Two clients, Harbour and Pine and Corvid Foods, have NDAs that do not allow third parties to process their work.

**Pilot group.** The four people who tested Lantern from 7 April to 2 May 2025: Hannah Frost, Daniel Reyes, Samir Haddad and Leo Park.

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Red data.** Client contracts, personal data and financial records. It may go into Lantern only with written approval from Tomasz Lewandowski.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

**Token.** A piece of a word. Models read and write in tokens; about four characters make one token in English.

**Workspace.** A separate folder of documents and conversations for one client project. A document uploaded to one workspace cannot be seen from another.

BRIGHTWATER STUDIO
DATA HANDLING STANDARD FOR LANTERN
Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

This standard says where Lantern keeps data, how long, and how it is removed. It supports the AI use policy, which sets the rules for people. Where the two seem to differ, the policy wins and Tomasz must be told.

1. WHERE DATA LIVES

1.1 Everything Lantern stores is on lantern-01, in the locked comms cupboard. Nothing is stored with an outside provider except the weekly encrypted backup copy (see section 5).

1.2 There are three data folders on lantern-01:
    - /srv/lantern/uploads holds documents that staff upload into a project workspace.
    - /srv/lantern/chat_logs holds one file per day with the conversations people had.
    - /srv/lantern/audit holds the audit log.

1.3 The audit log records who asked, when, in which workspace, and how many tokens the answer used. It never records the text of a prompt or of an answer.

2. ACCESS

2.1 Lantern can be reached only from the office network, subnet 192.168.10.0/24. No port is open to the internet.

2.2 Every person has an individual account. Shared accounts are not allowed.

2.3 There are two administrators, Priya Nair and Tomasz Lewandowski. Both use multi-factor sign-in. Administrators can read the audit log and disable accounts. They do not read chat logs unless Tomasz opens an incident.

3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

sources.title: incident-runbook.md
sources.section: Lantern incident runbook > What to do, in order
sources.text:
## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

Brightwater Studio. Notes kept by Daniel Reyes.

3 March 2025: Kickoff
Present: Maya Okafor, Daniel Reyes, Priya Nair, Tomasz Lewandowski, Hannah Frost, Samir Haddad.

Present: Maya Okafor, Daniel Reyes, Tomasz Lewandowski, Hannah Frost.

- Tomasz proposed keeping chat logs for 30 days, to keep the amount of stored client material small.
- Hannah said designers go back to a client thread up to three months later, for example when a client returns after a pause, and a 30 day limit would lose that context.
- Maya agreed with Hannah.

Decisions
- Chat logs are kept for 90 days, not 30.
- Audit logs, which hold no conversation text, are kept for a year.

Actions
- Tomasz Lewandowski: update the draft and send it to Maya.

sources.title: data-handling-standard.txt
sources.text:
3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

    Chat logs ............................ 90 days
    Audit logs ........................... 365 days
    Uploaded documents ................... until the project is closed, plus 12 months
    Backups .............................. 30 days
    Incident records ..................... three years

3.2 A chat log is removed by the nightly retention job at 02:30, once it is more than 90 days old. Uploaded documents are not removed by the job. The operations lead, Daniel Reyes, removes them by hand when a project has been closed for 12 months, and records the date.

3.3 Because backups are kept for 30 days, a chat log that has just been deleted can still exist in a backup for up to 30 days. The longest a chat can therefore survive anywhere is 120 days.

4. LEGAL HOLD

4.1 To stop deletion during an incident, create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it is there the retention job deletes nothing.

4.2 Only Tomasz Lewandowski may order the file to be removed, after the incident review.

5. BACKUPS

5.1 A backup runs every night at 01:00 to the office NAS.

5.2 Every Sunday at 03:00 an encrypted copy goes to cloud storage in an EU region. The key stays in the office safe.

5.3 A restore is tested once a year. The first test, on 2 May 2025, restored 310 GB in 47 minutes.

6. DELETION

6.1 Deleting a file means removing it from the disk. Lantern keeps no recycle bin.

sources.section: Lantern incident runbook > How serious is it?
sources.text:
## How serious is it?

| Level | What it means | Acknowledge | Contain | Tell the client |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Red data exposed, or Lantern compromised | within 15 minutes | within 1 hour | within 24 hours |
| S2 | Amber data exposed, or a wrong output reached a client | within 4 hours | the same working day | within 72 hours, if their data was involved |
| S3 | An outage or a small breach of the rules with no data exposed | the next working day | within 3 working days | no notice needed |

An S3 incident is discussed at the weekly project meeting. S1 and S2 incidents get a review meeting.

sources.section: Lantern incident runbook > What to do, in order
sources.text:
## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

Memo: Which way should Brightwater 
run an AI assistant?  
To: Maya Okafor 
From: Daniel Reyes 
Date: 28 February 2025 
Decision wanted: at the kickoff meeting on 3 March 2025 
Recommendation 
I recommend Option C, a computer of our own running the assistant in the office. It is the 
most expensive of the three, but it is the only one that keeps client work inside the building, 
and two of our clients require that. 
The three options 
Option A: a cloud subscription 
Each person pays £22 per user per month. For 12 people that is £264 per month, or £3,168 
for the year. Nothing has to be bought or looked after. Our prompts and documents would 
be processed by the provider, in an EU region. 
Option B: a hosted private instance 
A provider in the UK runs an assistant for us alone at a flat £780 per month, or £9,360 for 
the year. Our data stays with that provider. Corvid Foods would have to agree to a change in 
its NDA first. 
Option C: a workstation in our own office 
A one-off cost of £2,330 (£2,150 for the workstation and £180 for a UPS battery unit) and 
£1,244 per month (a support retainer of £1,200, about £35 of electricity and £9 of cloud 
storage for backups). The first year costs £17,258. The second year would cost £14,928, 
because the one-off cost does not come back. Data never leaves the building.

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Red data.** Client contracts, personal data and financial records. It may go into Lantern only with written approval from Tomasz Lewandowski.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

## What to do, in order

1. **Stop it.** Priya or Tomasz disables the affected account in the admin console. If a tool outside Lantern is involved, stop using it.
2. **Record it.** Add a row to the incident log (a CSV file in the ops folder) with the next INC number, the date, the level, who reported it and a one-line summary.
3. **Preserve the evidence.** Create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the nightly retention job deletes nothing, so the logs you need cannot expire.
4. **Tell the right people.** Tomasz decides who must be told. Maya speaks to the client. Nobody else contacts a client about an incident.
5. **Fix it.** Priya or the owner of the affected system makes the repair and notes what was changed.
6. **Review it.** Tomasz holds a review within 5 working days of the incident being contained. Only after he signs off is the LEGAL_HOLD file removed.

sources.text:
# Lantern glossary

Short definitions of the words you will meet in the Lantern documents at Brightwater Studio.

**Amber data.** Client work in progress and internal plans. Lantern may process it. Outside AI tools may not.

**Audit log.** A record of who used Lantern, when, in which workspace and how many tokens were used. It never contains the text of a prompt or an answer. Kept for 365 days.

**Cleanup job.** The script log_cleanup.py that runs on lantern-01 every night at 02:30 and deletes chat logs and audit logs that have passed their retention period.

**Embedder.** The small model that turns a document into numbers so that Lantern can search it by meaning. It runs on the processor, not on the graphics card.

**First-token time.** How long you wait before the first word of an answer appears. The studio's target is under 3 seconds for 95 percent of requests.

**Green data.** Published or public material, such as marketing copy that is already on the website. Anyone may use it with any tool.

**Lantern.** The private AI assistant that runs on the workstation lantern-01. It is the result of Project Lantern.

**Legal hold.** An empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the cleanup job deletes nothing. Used during an incident so that evidence is kept.

**NDA.** A non-disclosure agreement. Two clients, Harbour and Pine and Corvid Foods, have NDAs that do not allow third parties to process their work.

**Pilot group.** The four people who tested Lantern from 7 April to 2 May 2025: Hannah Frost, Daniel Reyes, Samir Haddad and Leo Park.

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

BRIGHTWATER STUDIO
DATA HANDLING STANDARD FOR LANTERN
Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

This standard says where Lantern keeps data, how long, and how it is removed. It supports the AI use policy, which sets the rules for people. Where the two seem to differ, the policy wins and Tomasz must be told.

1. WHERE DATA LIVES

1.1 Everything Lantern stores is on lantern-01, in the locked comms cupboard. Nothing is stored with an outside provider except the weekly encrypted backup copy (see section 5).

1.2 There are three data folders on lantern-01:
    - /srv/lantern/uploads holds documents that staff upload into a project workspace.
    - /srv/lantern/chat_logs holds one file per day with the conversations people had.
    - /srv/lantern/audit holds the audit log.

1.3 The audit log records who asked, when, in which workspace, and how many tokens the answer used. It never records the text of a prompt or of an answer.

2.1 Lantern can be reached only from the office network, subnet 192.168.10.0/24. No port is open to the internet.

2.2 Every person has an individual account. Shared accounts are not allowed.

2.3 There are two administrators, Priya Nair and Tomasz Lewandowski. Both use multi-factor sign-in. Administrators can read the audit log and disable accounts. They do not read chat logs unless Tomasz opens an incident.

3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

## Scheduled jobs

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Every night at 01:00 | Backup to the office NAS |

sources.title: data-handling-standard.txt
sources.text:
3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

    Chat logs ............................ 90 days
    Audit logs ........................... 365 days
    Uploaded documents ................... until the project is closed, plus 12 months
    Backups .............................. 30 days
    Incident records ..................... three years

3.2 A chat log is removed by the nightly retention job at 02:30, once it is more than 90 days old. Uploaded documents are not removed by the job. The operations lead, Daniel Reyes, removes them by hand when a project has been closed for 12 months, and records the date.

3.3 Because backups are kept for 30 days, a chat log that has just been deleted can still exist in a backup for up to 30 days. The longest a chat can therefore survive anywhere is 120 days.

4. LEGAL HOLD

4.1 To stop deletion during an incident, create an empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it is there the retention job deletes nothing.

4.2 Only Tomasz Lewandowski may order the file to be removed, after the incident review.

5. BACKUPS

5.1 A backup runs every night at 01:00 to the office NAS.

5.2 Every Sunday at 03:00 an encrypted copy goes to cloud storage in an EU region. The key stays in the office safe.

5.3 A restore is tested once a year. The first test, on 2 May 2025, restored 310 GB in 47 minutes.

6. DELETION

6.1 Deleting a file means removing it from the disk. Lantern keeps no recycle bin.

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
# Lantern glossary

Short definitions of the words you will meet in the Lantern documents at Brightwater Studio.

**Amber data.** Client work in progress and internal plans. Lantern may process it. Outside AI tools may not.

**Audit log.** A record of who used Lantern, when, in which workspace and how many tokens were used. It never contains the text of a prompt or an answer. Kept for 365 days.

**Cleanup job.** The script log_cleanup.py that runs on lantern-01 every night at 02:30 and deletes chat logs and audit logs that have passed their retention period.

**Embedder.** The small model that turns a document into numbers so that Lantern can search it by meaning. It runs on the processor, not on the graphics card.

**First-token time.** How long you wait before the first word of an answer appears. The studio's target is under 3 seconds for 95 percent of requests.

**Green data.** Published or public material, such as marketing copy that is already on the website. Anyone may use it with any tool.

**Lantern.** The private AI assistant that runs on the workstation lantern-01. It is the result of Project Lantern.

**Legal hold.** An empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the cleanup job deletes nothing. Used during an incident so that evidence is kept.

**NDA.** A non-disclosure agreement. Two clients, Harbour and Pine and Corvid Foods, have NDAs that do not allow third parties to process their work.

**Pilot group.** The four people who tested Lantern from 7 April to 2 May 2025: Hannah Frost, Daniel Reyes, Samir Haddad and Leo Park.

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

sources.title: glossary.md
sources.text:
**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Red data.** Client contracts, personal data and financial records. It may go into Lantern only with written approval from Tomasz Lewandowski.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

**Token.** A piece of a word. Models read and write in tokens; about four characters make one token in English.

**Workspace.** A separate folder of documents and conversations for one client project. A document uploaded to one workspace cannot be seen from another.

sources.title: hardware-setup.md
sources.section: Lantern hardware and performance > The model
sources.text:
## The model

The assistant is an open-weight language model with 8 billion parameters. It is stored in 4-bit precision (the term is "quantised"), which brings it down to about 5 GB of video memory. The separate model that turns documents into searchable vectors, the embedder, runs on the processor instead, so the graphics card is left free for the chat model.

run an AI assistant?

Recommendation 
I recommend Option C, a computer of our own running the assistant in the office. It is the 
most expensive of the three, but it is the only one that keeps client work inside the building, 
and two of our clients require that. 
The three options 
Option A: a cloud subscription 
Each person pays £22 per user per month. For 12 people that is £264 per month, or £3,168 
for the year. Nothing has to be bought or looked after. Our prompts and documents would 
be processed by the provider, in an EU region.

A provider in the UK runs an assistant for us alone at a flat £780 per month, or £9,360 for

its NDA first.

A one-off cost of £2,330 (£2,150 for the workstation and £180 for a UPS battery unit) and 
£1,244 per month (a support retainer of £1,200, about £35 of electricity and £9 of cloud 
storage for backups). The first year costs £17,258. The second year would cost £14,928, 
because the one-off cost does not come back. Data never leaves the building.

BRIGHTWATER STUDIO
DATA HANDLING STANDARD FOR LANTERN
Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

This standard says where Lantern keeps data, how long, and how it is removed. It supports the AI use policy, which sets the rules for people. Where the two seem to differ, the policy wins and Tomasz must be told.

1. WHERE DATA LIVES

1.1 Everything Lantern stores is on lantern-01, in the locked comms cupboard. Nothing is stored with an outside provider except the weekly encrypted backup copy (see section 5).

1.2 There are three data folders on lantern-01:
    - /srv/lantern/uploads holds documents that staff upload into a project workspace.
    - /srv/lantern/chat_logs holds one file per day with the conversations people had.
    - /srv/lantern/audit holds the audit log.

1.3 The audit log records who asked, when, in which workspace, and how many tokens the answer used. It never records the text of a prompt or of an answer.

2. ACCESS

2.1 Lantern can be reached only from the office network, subnet 192.168.10.0/24. No port is open to the internet.

2.2 Every person has an individual account. Shared accounts are not allowed.

2.3 There are two administrators, Priya Nair and Tomasz Lewandowski. Both use multi-factor sign-in. Administrators can read the audit log and disable accounts. They do not read chat logs unless Tomasz opens an incident.

3. RETENTION

Version 1.1, 14 April 2025. Owner: Tomasz Lewandowski, security and privacy officer.

This standard says where Lantern keeps data, how long, and how it is removed. It supports the AI use policy, which sets the rules for people. Where the two seem to differ, the policy wins and Tomasz must be told.

1. WHERE DATA LIVES

1.1 Everything Lantern stores is on lantern-01, in the locked comms cupboard. Nothing is stored with an outside provider except the weekly encrypted backup copy (see section 5).

    - /srv/lantern/uploads holds documents that staff upload into a project workspace.
    - /srv/lantern/chat_logs holds one file per day with the conversations people had.

1.3 The audit log records who asked, when, in which workspace, and how many tokens the answer used. It never records the text of a prompt or of an answer.

2.1 Lantern can be reached only from the office network, subnet 192.168.10.0/24. No port is open to the internet.

2.2 Every person has an individual account. Shared accounts are not allowed.

2.3 There are two administrators, Priya Nair and Tomasz Lewandowski. Both use multi-factor sign-in. Administrators can read the audit log and disable accounts. They do not read chat logs unless Tomasz opens an incident.

3. RETENTION

3.1 The periods are:

sources.title: log_cleanup.py
sources.text:
"""Nightly retention job for Lantern (lantern-01).

Runs every night at 02:30 from cron. It deletes chat logs older than 90 days and audit logs
older than 365 days. It never touches uploaded documents: the operations lead removes those by
hand once a project has been closed for 12 months.

If the file /srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD exists the job deletes nothing, writes "hold active" to its
log and exits with code 3, so that whoever is handling an incident keeps the evidence.
"""

import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CHAT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/chat_logs")
AUDIT_LOG_DIR = Path("/srv/lantern/audit")
HOLD_FILE = Path("/srv/lantern/LEGAL_HOLD")
CLEANUP_LOG = Path("/var/log/lantern/cleanup.log")

CHAT_RETENTION_DAYS = 90
AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS = 365
SECONDS_PER_DAY = 86_400
EXIT_OK = 0
EXIT_HOLD = 3


def expired(directory: Path, max_age_days: int, now: float) -> list[Path]:
    """The .jsonl files in ``directory`` last changed more than ``max_age_days`` days ago.

    A file exactly ``max_age_days`` old is kept: the job deletes only what is older than the limit.
    """
    cutoff = now - max_age_days * SECONDS_PER_DAY
    return [path for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.jsonl")) if path.stat().st_mtime < cutoff]


def write_log(message: str) -> None:
    """Append one timestamped line to the cleanup log."""
    stamp = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    with CLEANUP_LOG.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        handle.write(f"{stamp} {message}\n")

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

**Red data.** Client contracts, personal data and financial records. It may go into Lantern only with written approval from Tomasz Lewandowski.

**Retention.** How long something is kept before it is deleted. Chat logs: 90 days.

**Severity levels.** S1 is the most serious incident (Red data exposed or Lantern compromised), S2 is Amber data exposed or a wrong output reaching a client, S3 is an outage or a small breach with no data exposed.

**Token.** A piece of a word. Models read and write in tokens; about four characters make one token in English.

**Workspace.** A separate folder of documents and conversations for one client project. A document uploaded to one workspace cannot be seen from another.

## The model

The assistant is an open-weight language model with 8 billion parameters. It is stored in 4-bit precision (the term is "quantised"), which brings it down to about 5 GB of video memory. The separate model that turns documents into searchable vectors, the embedder, runs on the processor instead, so the graphics card is left free for the chat model.

Short definitions of the words you will meet in the Lantern documents at Brightwater Studio.

**Amber data.** Client work in progress and internal plans. Lantern may process it. Outside AI tools may not.

**Audit log.** A record of who used Lantern, when, in which workspace and how many tokens were used. It never contains the text of a prompt or an answer. Kept for 365 days.

**Legal hold.** An empty file called LEGAL_HOLD in /srv/lantern. While it exists the cleanup job deletes nothing. Used during an incident so that evidence is kept.

**NDA.** A non-disclosure agreement. Two clients, Harbour and Pine and Corvid Foods, have NDAs that do not allow third parties to process their work.

**Pilot group.** The four people who tested Lantern from 7 April to 2 May 2025: Hannah Frost, Daniel Reyes, Samir Haddad and Leo Park.

**Quantised.** A model that has been stored with fewer bits per number so that it takes less memory. Lantern's model uses 4 bits and needs about 5 GB.

## Speed

Priya measured the speed on 31 March 2025, before the pilot:

- The median time to the first word of an answer was 1.8 seconds.
- The 95th percentile was 3.4 seconds. The target in the vendor memo had been under 3 seconds at the 95th percentile, so the first benchmark missed it.
- Text came out at 38 tokens per second.

On 14 April Priya shortened the context length to 4,096 tokens and measured again. The 95th percentile dropped to 2.8 seconds, inside the target.

PROJECT LANTERN: MEETING NOTES
Brightwater Studio. Notes kept by Daniel Reyes.

----------------------------------------------------------------
3 March 2025: Kickoff
Present: Maya Okafor, Daniel Reyes, Priya Nair, Tomasz Lewandowski, Hannah Frost, Samir Haddad.

Decisions
- Go ahead with a local assistant on one workstation, as recommended in the vendor memo of 28 February.
- Name of the project: Project Lantern.
- Daniel Reyes owns the project. Maya Okafor is the sponsor.

Actions
- Priya Nair: order the hardware by 17 March.
- Tomasz Lewandowski: draft the AI use policy for approval by 21 March.
- Samir Haddad: confirm the budget of 17,258 pounds for the first year.

----------------------------------------------------------------
10 March 2025: Policy draft
Present: Maya Okafor, Daniel Reyes, Tomasz Lewandowski, Hannah Frost.

Discussion
- Tomasz proposed keeping chat logs for 30 days, to keep the amount of stored client material small.
- Hannah said designers go back to a client thread up to three months later, for example when a client returns after a pause, and a 30 day limit would lose that context.
- Maya agreed with Hannah.

Decisions
- Chat logs are kept for 90 days, not 30.
- Audit logs, which hold no conversation text, are kept for a year.

Actions
- Tomasz Lewandowski: update the draft and send it to Maya.
